text: Is jealousy normal? And if it is, where exactly is the line between normal emotion and self-destruction? Let's break it down. So, is jealousy normal? Yes. If a woman has value for you, if you've been seeing each other for some time, or there's already a relationship, emotions are normal, concern is normal, and yes, even jealousy, to a certain degree, is normal. A man who feels absolutely nothing, who blindly assumes nothing bad can ever happen, lives in a fantasy world. We don't live in a pink harmless universe. Things happen, people cheat, temptations exist. Ignoring that completely is not maturity, it is naivety. So no, the goal is not to become emotionless. But here's where things go wrong. There are two extremes. One extreme is blindness and denial. The other extreme is obsession and self-destruction. And the second one is far more common. The problem starts when a man begins to mentally torture himself. She's not with you for one evening, and you can't sleep. You replay scenarios in your head. You imagine things she might be doing. You lose focus, appetite, and peace. At that point, jealousy is no longer a signal. It's a poison. And the question is, why does this happen? Very often the reason is simple. The woman plays a disproportionately large role in your life. For many men, even early in dating, the woman becomes the center of everything. Sometimes even the only meaningful thing. And when that happens, fear becomes inevitable. If you lose her, you lose everything. Because there is nothing else. That is not how a healthy life is structured. A woman should not be the first place in your life, especially at the beginning. First place should be you yourself, your ambitions and your goals. Second place, your passions, interests, things that give you energy. Only then comes a woman. When your life is full, jealousy loses its grip. You don't see that home spiraling because you actually have things to do. A man with direction doesn't emotionally collapse every time his girlfriend leaves the house. The second major issue is self-esteem. Many jealous men don't actually believe they are valuable. Deep down they think, if she gets a chance, she will leave me. Why would she stay loyal to me? That's not because of her behavior. That's because of how they see themselves. The good news is this. You can build your self-esteem up. When you set goals in life and move towards them, when you collect small and big wins, confidence grows naturally. And with it, jealousy weakens. And finally, the third point, knowledge and realism. If you understand how relationships actually work, if you can read behavior instead of inventing fantasies, jealousy becomes manageable. You stop reacting to imaginary threats and start relying on facts. Has she shown interest? Does she communicate? Does her behavior match her words? How does she act towards you consistently? Facts calm the mind. Fantasies destroy it. So if you want jealousy to stop ruining your life, remember three things. First, a woman is not the center of your existence. Second, self-respect must be built through action. Third, use logic, not imagination. Less panic, less fantasy, more structure. Then jealousy becomes what it should be. A signal you can understand, not a fire that burns you from the inside.
